data.body_html:
August in Marbella brings scorching 34°C heat on land, but a Marbella boat rental offers the ultimate escape. With sea breezes, air-conditioned cabins, and unlimited chilled drinks, you can beat the heat in style. Our fleet departs from Puerto Banús, minutes from the cool Mediterranean waters. Here’s how to stay comfortable and make the most of your August charter.

Why a Boat Beats the Beach in August

On land, the heat can be oppressive, especially between 12:00 and 16:00. On the water, the constant breeze and evaporation cool you by 5-8°C. You can swim directly from the boat, anchor in shaded coves like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés, and retreat to air-conditioned interiors. All our charters include cold drinks, ice, and light snacks—no queuing for overpriced beach bars.

Our Fleet: Which Yacht Keeps You Coolest?

For August, larger yachts with enclosed, air-conditioned saloons are ideal. The Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) has a spacious main deck with full AC. The Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) offers both shaded flybridge and cool interior. For smaller groups, the Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) has a cabin with AC. Even the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) has a bimini top and forward sunpad shade. See our full fleet on the [Marbella boat rental](/) page.

Pricing That Includes Everything

All our prices include skipper, fuel, insurance, Spanish IVA (21%), and drinks. For August, the all-inclusive nature means no hidden costs. Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) cost €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours. Mangusta 80 charters start at €4,719 for 4 hours and include a free jet ski. For other boats like the Pershing 46 or Fairline Targa 12m, pricing is on request via WhatsApp.

Best Anchorages for Swimming and Cooling Off

  • Cala del Faro – sheltered cove, calm water, perfect for a midday swim.
  • Cala Cortés – near Cabopino, with sandy beach and shallow waters.
  • Cabopino – lively beach club, easy to anchor and dinghy ashore.
  • Río Verde – quiet spot near Marbella, good for snorkelling.

All our boats have swim platforms and ladders. The sea temperature in August is 24-26°C, ideal for long swims.

What to Bring and Wear

Pack high-SPF reef-safe sunscreen, a wide-brimmed hat, polarized sunglasses, and a light cover-up. We provide towels on request. The boat has shaded areas, but the sun is intense. A rash vest or UV-protective shirt is recommended for kids. Don’t forget a camera—the views of La Concha mountain from the sea are stunning.

Booking Tips for August

August is peak season, so book 2-3 weeks ahead. WhatsApp is the fastest way to confirm availability. For larger groups (up to 12 pax), the Mangusta 80 or Ferretti 94 are best. For a romantic couple’s trip, the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax) are affordable options. All departures from Puerto Banús, with free parking nearby.
